deep.reconstruction: Context: this is a section on Hilbertian exterior powers of operators. For Hilbert spaces E and F, Λ̂^n E denotes the completion of Λ^n E for the Hilbert structure (a_1∧…∧a_n, b_1∧…∧b_n) = det((a_i, b_j)). For operators u_i ∈ L(E,F), u_1∧…∧u_n is the induced map, and Λ̂u = u∧…∧u. The previous page proved three formulas. (10): Λ̂v ∘ Λ̂u = Λ̂(v∘u). (11): (Λ̂u)* = Λ̂(u*). (12): (Λ̂h)^α = Λ̂(h^α) for h ≥ 0 and α > 0. It began the positivity argument: write h = k² with k ≥ 0 hermitian. This page finishes the proof. (i) Since Λ̂k is hermitian, Λ̂h = (Λ̂k)² is a positive hermitian operator. (ii) The formula (12), which the page calls (11), holds for integer α by multiplicativity. It holds for α = 1/n because (Λ̂h^{1/n})^n = Λ̂h and Λ̂h^{1/n} is positive, so uniqueness of positive n-th roots gives Λ̂(h^{1/n}) = (Λ̂h)^{1/n}. Combining the two cases gives all positive rationals. (iii) α ↦ H^α is norm-continuous on α > 0 for positive H, and u ↦ Λ̂u is continuous (a homogeneous polynomial map of degree n, Lipschitz on bounded sets). So both sides are continuous in α, agree on the rationals, and hence agree for all α > 0. The page then summarises as Proposition 1. If u_i ∈ L(E,F), then u_1∧…∧u_n is continuous for the pre-Hilbert structures and extends to Λ̂^n E → Λ̂^n F with norm ≤ ∏‖u_i‖. The map u ↦ Λ̂u from L(E) to L(Λ̂^n E) is multiplicative, commutes with *, and preserves hermitian, unitary and positive operators (with the power formula). Purpose: preparation for Proposition 2 on the next page. If u is compact then Λ^n u is compact, with eigenvalues the products λ_{i1}…λ_{in} for i1 < … < in. This is the standard tool for Weyl-type eigenvalue/singular-value inequalities and Fredholm determinants. Note |Λ̂u| = Λ̂|u| follows from (11)–(12) with α = 1/2. This material feeds Grothendieck's 1953–56 work on nuclear operators and Fredholm theory.
errors: Formula numbering slip: the page calls the power formula '(11)', but on the previous page it is numbered (12); (11) there is (Λ̂u)* = Λ̂u*.

Minor gap: the continuity argument needs α ↦ H^α to be continuous in operator norm (true for α > 0 via the continuous functional calculus, uniformly on compact α-intervals). It also needs continuity of the nonlinear map u ↦ Λ̂u, which is only implicitly justified (a polynomial map with ‖Λ̂u − Λ̂v‖ ≤ n·max(‖u‖,‖v‖)^{n−1}‖u−v‖). Both are fine.
The direct proof via functional calculus or spectral theorem would be shorter, but the argument given is correct.

ideas.what: Hilbertian exterior power Λ̂^n E and functoriality u ↦ Λ̂^n u, with norm bound ‖u_1∧…∧u_n‖ ≤ ∏‖u_i‖
ideas.modern_name: Exterior powers of Hilbert spaces / antisymmetric Fock space functor Γ_a
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (H. Weyl 1949 for eigenvalue inequalities; second-quantization literature, Segal, Cook 1950s)
ideas.where_published: Possibly used implicitly in 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) and 'Produits tensoriels topologiques' (Mem. AMS 1955); unsure of explicit Hilbert treatment

ideas.what: Λ̂ commutes with adjoints, preserves positivity, and (Λ̂h)^α = Λ̂(h^α), proved via roots, then rationals, then continuity
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the second-quantization functor Γ with continuous functional calculus (e.g. |Λu| = Λ|u|)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; standard in matrix analysis (Bhatia, Matrix Analysis) and Simon's Trace Ideals

ideas.what: Proposition 1: Λ̂ is multiplicative, *-preserving, and maps hermitian, unitary and positive operators to the same classes
ideas.modern_name: Γ_a as a *-multiplicative (non-linear) map L(E) → L(Λ^n E)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard foundational lemmas on exterior powers of Hilbert-space operators, preparing Weyl/Fredholm-type eigenvalue results. Historically interesting as a trace of Grothendieck's 1953 route to Fredholm theory, but mathematically routine and well documented elsewhere.
transcription_corrections: The formula referred to as '(11)' on this page is the power formula numbered (12) on the previous page; the reference is an author slip, not a transcription error.
The notation varies between Λ̂ (hat) here and Λ̄ on the previous page; it likely denotes the same completed exterior power.

Opening struck line '[-des formes hermitiennes, ou hermitiennes-] pr. K': probably 'puisque Λ̂k est hermitien, il s'ensuit bien que Λ̂h est, comme carré d'un hermitien, un hermitien positif' — the image reads closer to 'comme carré d'un hermitien' than 'comme h une hermitienne'.
'hermitiens, unitaires [?] et opérateurs positifs' is plausibly correct ('les hermitiens, unitaires et hermitiens positifs').
